candidate: STM-0395 — I keep chasing unavailable people.
chain: C1 phenomenology 'I always care more than they do' (STM-0256/0257) / feeling like an option → Exploration → Discernment → Role Functioning → Reciprocity → candidate: increasing pursuit toward the withholding → relevance: pacing effort to observed reciprocity materially improves reading who reciprocates.
relationship: Directly operationalizes observing reciprocity before investing — a core Discernment act.
target: Notice when you increase effort toward someone becoming less available; pace effort to what is reciprocated.
duplicates: No — C1's only approved Play is CP-18 (intentional dating breaks).
context: You still get to feel drawn to someone; this is pacing, not withholding affection.
may_say: If you notice you give more when the other person gives less, you can slow down and watch whether they show up too.
may_not_say: Do NOT say people who feel unchosen chase unavailable people (prevalence), or that they chase out of fear of not being chosen (mechanism).

candidate: STM-0042 — I always date emotionally unavailable people.
chain: C1 'feel like the backup / never first choice' → Exploration → Discernment → Trust → Availability → candidate: selecting emotionally-unavailable partners → relevance: weighting demonstrated availability in selection improves Discernment.
relationship: Selecting for availability is central to Discernment.
target: Weigh how available and consistent someone actually is when deciding who to invest in.
context: Source is somewhat pattern-level ('always date X'); the discrete lever is selection-weighting. Attraction still matters.
may_say: If you tend to invest in people who stay hard to reach, you can give more weight to people who show up steadily.
may_not_say: Do NOT attribute this pattern to C1 people as a group, or infer a fear/attachment cause.

candidate: STM-0396 — I ignore people who would probably treat me well.
chain: C1 'never the first choice / feel replaceable' → Exploration → Discernment → Role Functioning → Intentionality → candidate: dismissing available/kind people → relevance: not foreclosing available options before evaluating them improves Discernment.
relationship: Keeps viable options open long enough to evaluate compatibility — a Discernment act.
target: When brushing off someone kind and available, tell 'no real spark' apart from 'unfamiliar', and give a little more observation before deciding.
context: Real attraction still matters; not an instruction to date people you aren't drawn to.
may_say: If you lose interest in people who are steady and available, you can pause and give it a little more time before deciding.
may_not_say: Do NOT claim C1 people dismiss good partners, or infer self-sabotage.

chain: C1 'keep hoping they'll change their mind' (STM-0442) / 'waiting for them to choose me' (0440) → Exploration → Discernment → Role Functioning → Boundaries → candidate: open-ended staying → relevance: a see-by point converts open-ended hope into an evidence-based decision.
relationship: Turns passive waiting into a decision — a Discernment act.
target: Set, in advance, what you need to see and by when; then decide from what actually happened.
duplicates: No. STM-0556 supports the SAME target — treat as ONE proposed application.
context: Depends on whether real change is happening vs only hope.
may_say: If you wait a long time hoping someone will decide about you, you can set a point by which you need to see something real, then decide.
may_not_say: Do NOT say C1 people stay too long, or infer why.

candidate: STM-0556 — I always give people one more chance.
chain: Mirrors C1's hope-then-disappointment cycle (STM-0522–0531) → Exploration → Discernment → Trust → Accountability → candidate: open-ended repeated chances → relevance: tying a chance to observable change supports Discernment.
target: Tie any further chance to one specific, observable change within a timeframe (SAME target as STM-0039).
duplicates: Consolidates with STM-0039 into a single see-by-date application.
context: Repair vs enabling depends on demonstrated accountability.
may_say: If you keep giving chances while nothing changes, you can name one real change you need to see, and by when.

candidate: STM-1039 — I'm watching to see if their actions match what they promised.
source: 24 — Difficulty Knowing Whether to Invest (EXCLUSIVITY — cross-phase)
chain: C1 'waiting for them to choose me' (0440) → Exploration → Discernment → Trust → Congruence (exists in Exploration) → candidate: observing action–word congruence → relevance: replaces passive waiting with active observation of congruence. SOURCE IS EXCLUSIVITY PHASE (Rule 5 → stronger scrutiny).
relationship: The adaptive Discernment behavior itself (Likely-Adaptive-Already in its home cluster).
target: Instead of waiting to be chosen, watch whether their actions match their words over time.
context: Cross-phase source (Exclusivity → Exploration); could tip into hypervigilance if extreme.
may_say: Instead of waiting for someone to choose you, you can watch whether what they do matches what they say.
may_not_say: No prevalence/mechanism; do not present as fixing a flaw — it is a positive pathway.
